brief: Richardsonian Romanesque commercial block of 1892: a two-storey rusticated stone front with blind arches over the upper windows, an arched attic window in a central gable and a balustraded parapet with the name carved in the frieze; two modern storefronts below with striped awnings.

floors: W W W W W W
facade.notes: the McKenzie-Kabic Block (Bowling Green OH, 1892): a two-storey rock-faced stone double front with the two owners' names in panels under a balustraded parapet, arched windows; the ground floor today: a pizza parlour with a striped awning and an ice-cream shop's 'COMING SOON' sign; a traffic signal and decorative lamp posts, bike racks

why.note: the two-part block: shops below, offices or flats above
two owners' names on a shared front: two buildings built as one
